title: Shell parity scenario
description: Inputs of one server-versus-shell parity scenario: a seed log, then requests run at fixed instants. The server's answers are the oracle (goldens are recorded by SHELL-P1 into fixtures/shell-parity/golden/<id>.json and are not part of this contract); the shell's LocalApi must give the same answers after the normalisation of SHELL.md 8.3. SHELL.md section 8 is normative for how both harnesses run a scenario.

title.description: One line: what the scenario shows.
examples: Queue counts are the same with and without keep going (ADR-033)

covers.description: Coverage tags `<area>.<case>`. The mandatory tags are listed in SHELL.md 8.4; check.sh fails when one of them is covered by no scenario.

narrative.description: Human explanation, one step per line. Not used by harnesses.

clock_ms.description: The instant the seed is applied at: both harnesses set their injected clock to it while seeding. Every seed op has wall(hlc) <= clock_ms and every seeded reviewed_at <= clock_ms; every step has at_ms > clock_ms.

device_id.description: The device under test: the paired device the steps run as. Server harness: a device registered with this id whose token (read, write, review) sends the step requests. Shell harness: sync_state.device_id of the store LocalApi runs on. Never the minting device of a seed op.

dict_entries.description: JMdict sequence numbers the scenario relies on (every entry_seq in the seed and in step bodies, every e:<seq> deck item). Each must exist in fixtures/dict/JMdict_subset.xml, the dictionary both harnesses load. Ascending.

settings.description: The effective settings after the seed, for the reader: key -> value. It is an index, not an input: harnesses do not apply it. check.sh requires it to equal the last-writer-wins fold of the seed log's settings.set ops (highest hlc per key); keys never set are absent and have their defaults (SCHEMA.md section 6).

seed.description: The state before the first step.

device_id.description: The device that minted every seed op and every `apply` op (another paired device, 'A'). Differs from the scenario's device_id.

log.description: Ops in pushed form (contracts/sync/op.schema.json without seq and caused_by_op_id), client-emittable types only, all minted by seed.device_id, in strictly increasing hlc order. May be empty (the empty replica). Server harness: POST /sync/push as seed.device_id, in order, every op must be `accepted`. Shell harness: applied in order through the core pull-apply path with seq = 1, 2, ... and caused_by_op_id = null.

operations.description: operationIds of ../openapi.yaml the request steps call, ascending. Derived (check.sh recomputes it from the steps); lets a harness skip a scenario whose operations are not implemented yet. Every one is `local` or `local_or_proxy` in ops.json.

steps.description: Run in order. at_ms never decreases.

invariants.description: Cross-step facts the golden must satisfy; checked by SHELL-P1 when it records and by SHELL-P2 on the shell's answers.

equal.description: The values at these places (normalised response bodies) are equal as JSON. A pointer that does not resolve fails the invariant.

step.description: Index into `steps` (0-based) of a request step.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer into that step's response body; no `*`.

instant_ms.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC; not before FLOOR (2020-01-01).

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. `""` is the whole document.

seed_op.description: One op. Validated by check.sh against contracts/sync/op.schema.json (envelope and payload), plus: no seq, no caused_by_op_id, emitter `client`, device_id = seed.device_id, entity_id derived as ops/index.json says.

at_ms.description: Both harnesses set their injected clock to this instant before sending the request and keep it there until the answer (server: the clock behind now(), HLC physical time and the queue's day; shell: the device clock).

request.description: The request, in the shape of a bridge `req` (bridge.schema.json).

path.description: Path under /api/v1 (shell operations are not parity-tested: they have no server side).

query.description: Raw query string without `?`; `""` for none.

body.description: JSON request body as a value, or null for none. Sent as compact JSON with `content-type: application/json`.

ignore.description: JSON Pointers removed from this step's response body on both sides before comparing (SHELL.md 8.3 step 6). A reference token `*` matches every member of an object and every element of an array. Each entry needs a reason in `narrative`.

expect.description: What the contract already fixes about the answer. SHELL-P1 fails to record a golden that contradicts it (then the scenario or the server is wrong: CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST); SHELL-P2 gets it for free through the golden.

field_error.description: `errors[]` contains an element with this pointer (and this code, when given).

body.description: JSON Pointer -> the exact JSON value the response body has there.

lengths.description: JSON Pointer -> length of the array there.

absent.description: JSON Pointers that must not resolve (member omitted).

apply_step.description: Ops of another device arrive between two requests. Server harness: POST /sync/push as seed.device_id with the clock at at_ms; every op must be `accepted`. Shell harness: applied through the core pull-apply path, seq continuing after the highest seq used so far.

apply.description: Ops as in seed.log, with wall(hlc) <= at_ms and hlc above every earlier op of seed.device_id.
